title: Safety Pulse Orchestrator for Contextual SLO Triggers
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
We are building the Safety Pulse Orchestrator: a lightweight runtime component that synthesizes multi-signal SLO observations (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput) and issues contextual auto-rollback triggers during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. The orchestrator applies cohort-aware baselining, hysteresis windows, and an adaptive threshold scheduler so rollback decisions are robust to traffic shifts and transient noise.

Background and motivation:
Existing canary rules are static: single-metric thresholds or fixed percent deltas that generate noisy rollbacks during traffic spikes or when token-cost varies by request. Teams need an automated guard that understands cohort baselines (e.g., high-seq vs low-seq traffic), supports shadow traffic calibration, and reduces false positives while still providing fast protection for customer-facing regressions.

Goals:
- Detect regressions across latency, error-rate, token-cost, and throughput with a single composite score.
- Make triggers contextual by partitioning signals by traffic cohort (model input length, route, tenant).
- Provide tunable hysteresis and grace windows to avoid rolling back for short transients.
- Enable shadow-mode validation and synthetic probes before enabling auto-evacuation.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace long-term risk policy for cross-region failover.
- Not implementing RBAC UI; ops will toggle via API/CLI initially.

Proposed approach (technical):
1) Signal ingestion: Extend metrics exporter to feed per-request token-cost and route tags into the pulse service. Aggregate into sliding windows (1m/5m/15m) per-cohort.
2) Composite scoring: For each cohort compute z-score normalized deviations for latency, error rate, and cost relative to cohort baseline. Combine with weighted sum: Score = w_lat*Z_lat + w_err*Z_err + w_cost*Z_cost - w_thr*(throughput_change_factor).
3) Adaptive thresholds: Use an initial calibration (2-4 hours of shadow traffic) to set percentile-based thresholds (e.g., 99th-latency delta, 95th error-rate multiplier). Thresholds decay slowly to adapt to seasonality.
4) Hysteresis & safety windows: Require score > threshold for 2 consecutive 1-minute buckets OR sudden spike > emergency-bound to trigger immediate rollback.
5) Rollback action: On trigger, orchestrator can (configurable): revert traffic weight to previous stable model, divert new requests to fallback model, or pause rollout and create an incident with prefilled context.

Threshold tuning strategy:
- Bootstrap with conservative multipliers (to minimize false positives) during first 24h of a new rollout.
- Run automated parameter search in staging (grid over weights and window lengths) using historical traces & synthetic regressions to identify Pareto frontier of detection latency vs false positive rate. Target false-positive rate <5% while detection time <2 minutes for high-severity regressions.
- Expose quick heuristics in console: safe/default/aggressive profiles.

Observability and metrics:
- Expose composite_score, per-cohort Z-scores, detection_latency, and rollback_count metrics to Console dashboard.
- Attach sample request traces (span ids) for the minute window that caused the trigger.
- Emit an audit event with reason, impacted cohorts, and chosen rollback action.

Rollout plan:
Stage 0: Shadow-only runs for two weeks on non-prod tenants + synthetic regressions (complete).
Stage 1: Low-risk prod rollouts (1% traffic) with auto-alerts enabled, but auto-evacuation disabled (manual approval required).
Stage 2: Enable conservative auto-evacuation for Canary experiments with safety fences.
Stage 3: Gradually enable for A/B tests with tenant opt-in; monitor false positive rate and operator feedback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Orchestrator calculates composite_score and stores per-cohort sliding windows for all active rollouts.
- Simulated regression (introduced 40% latency increase for one cohort) is detected within 2 minutes in staging and generates audit event.
- False positive rate measured over a 72h shadow run stays below 5% with default profile.
- Rollback API successfully reverts traffic to previous stable model in under 30s in integration tests.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overfitting thresholds to historical traces can miss novel failure modes. Mitigation: keep conservative defaults and require shadow validation.
- Additional metric ingestion increases cardinality; we will limit cohorts to a fixed tagging scheme and TTL windows to bound memory.

Progress updates and decisions (chronological):
- 2025-02-05: Spike completed. Prototype pulse scoring library implemented (python) and validated on replay of last 30 days of production traces.
- 2025-02-12: Architecture review with SRE and PM. Decided to keep control plane logic in a separate service (pulse-orchestrator) and push minimal control API to routing layer.
- 2025-02-18: Shadow-only runs enabled in staging across 3 routes; dashboard started collecting composite_score metrics.
- 2025-02-24: Simulation results: conservative profile detected injected latency regressions within median 95s, false positive rate 3.2% on 48h synthetic workload.
- 2025-02-26: PR opened for Go implementation of scoring engine (https://github.com/redwood-inference/pulse/pull/42). 2 reviewers requested.
- 2025-02-28: Integration tests for rollback API are green in CI (branch pulse/integration).

Open questions / blockers:
- Need SRE sign-off on emergency rollback action semantics (hot revert vs throttle) — scheduled meeting 2025-03-03.
- Small perf regression noticed when enabling per-request token-cost tagging at 10K RPS; infra changes may be required to avoid metric ingestion backpressure.

- Complete PR review and merge scoring engine.
- Run a controlled 1% prod roll (Stage 1) behind feature flag and collect 7-day FP/TP metrics.
